concepts.title: Sources of Light and Straight-line Travel
concepts.section: Sources of light and straight line
concepts.definition: The sun, stars, fireflies and flames make their own light as luminous sources, and light from them travels in straight lines, a fact proven by seeing a candle only through holes kept in one line.
concepts.key_idea: Light goes straight until something turns it: this simple rule builds shadows, images and cameras.

concepts.title: Transparent, Translucent, Opaque and Shadows
concepts.definition: Glass lets light pass fully as a transparent material, butter paper partially as translucent, and wood not at all as opaque; where an opaque body blocks light, a dark shadow forms, with umbra and penumbra bands.
concepts.key_idea: What light cannot pass becomes shadow: the material's honesty to light decides the darkness behind it.

concepts.title: Reflection and the Plane Mirror
concepts.definition: Light bouncing off a smooth mirror obeys reflection: the angle of bounce equals the angle of arrival, and a plane mirror forms an image that is upright, same-sized, and laterally inverted, left becoming right.
concepts.formula: angle of incidence = angle of reflection
concepts.key_idea: A mirror obeys two quiet laws: equal angles and a faithful but left-right flipped image.

concepts.title: The Pinhole Camera and Useful Items
concepts.definition: A small hole in a dark box casts an inverted, real image on the far wall, the pinhole camera principle; the same ray ideas make useful items, periscopes, kaleidoscopes and solar cookers, from plain mirrors and angles.
concepts.key_idea: Straight rays plus a tiny hole give a true, upside-down picture: the simplest camera has no lens at all.
